title: Best Records On Time Alternatives for 2026
summary: Comparing Records On Time alternatives? See how Codes Health, Lexitas, Ontellus, RRS, and others compare on completeness, AI chronologies, integrations, and pricing.
body_markdown:
When you're weighing Records On Time alternatives, retrieval speed is only part of the picture. Complete records, AI-powered analysis, and workflow integration decide whether medical documentation becomes a case asset or a bottleneck. Records On Time built its reputation on EHR-connected retrieval, but many firms now want alternatives that pair document acquisition with intelligent analysis and automated chronologies. This guide walks through the top Records On Time alternatives, with a close look at how[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) combines medical record retrieval, AI-generated chronologies, potential breach-of-care flagging, and missing-record identification.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


Codes Health stands out as a leading Records On Time alternative, combining retrieval, AI-generated chronologies, potential breach-of-care flagging, and missing-record identification, with company-reported figures of[80% less manual review](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) (individual results may vary)


-


Same-day speed and completeness are separate criteria. Codes Health's position is that same-day services often don't get the complete records and need client involvement, which leads to churn; Codes Health advertises retrieval in a couple of weeks with completeness checks


-


Bundled chronologies may reduce separate purchasing needs, depending on the firm's review requirements and service agreement


-


General AI platforms like ChatGPT aren't designed for litigation-grade medical record review; Codes Health pairs purpose-built analysis with human review, and findings should still be checked against source records


-


Workflow integration matters: Codes Health's Filevine partnership lets firms manage retrieval without leaving their case management system, with custom integrations for high-volume firms


-


Several alternatives now offer AI summaries or chronologies, so compare outputs, review processes, and pricing directly


## **What is Records On Time and Why Teams Consider Alternatives**


Records On Time operates as a CMS-integrated medical record retrieval service, now part of the Rob Levine Legal Solutions family. Built by a personal injury attorney with 25+ years of experience, the platform emphasizes direct case management system delivery and electronic health record connectivity.


**Records On Time Core Offerings:**


-


Advertised access to 400,000+ EHR-connected providers


-


Direct integration with 7 case management systems (Neos, Needles, SmartAdvocate, Litify, Filevine, Clio, CASEpeer)


-


Advertised $49.95 retrieval service fee; eligible EHR retrievals have no provider fees, while traditional requests may involve additional provider charges


-


Records On Time states that it has completed SOC 2 Type I and Type II examinations; request current reports to verify scope


-


No contracts and no monthly subscription fee, as advertised


**Why Firms Evaluate Alternatives:**


Records On Time's offering centers on retrieval and CMS delivery. Plaintiff firms handling complex medical malpractice, mass torts, or high-volume personal injury caseloads often want platforms that also provide:


-


Automated medical chronologies organized by clinical visit


-


Potential breach-of-care flags for expert review preparation


-


Missing record identification before settlement negotiations begin


-


Flags for apparent gaps in the available treatment history


-


Future medical expense extraction for damages work


Records On Time's same-day EHR option depends on provider connectivity and completed client authorization. Ask each vendor how it checks requested providers, date ranges, and record types, and how it handles missing materials. Codes Health's position is that same-day services often don't get the complete records, and filling the gaps requires client involvement that frustrates clients and leads to churn.


The eight alternatives below are listed to help you compare service models. Codes Health is our featured pick.


## **1. Codes Health**


Codes Health combines medical record retrieval, AI-generated chronologies, potential breach-of-care flagging, and missing-record identification, functioning as a pre-litigation department for plaintiff firms. It retrieves records through claims clearinghouses, custodian integrations, proprietary provider networks, patient portals, fax, email, and phone, then applies purpose-built AI to extract case-relevant insights.


**Key Codes Health Capabilities:**


-


AI-generated medical chronologies organized by clinical visit


-


Potential breach-of-care flags for attorney and expert review


-


Proactive missing record detection that identifies documentation gaps before delivery


-


Human verification layer where medical and legal specialists review AI outputs


-


Flags for apparent gaps in the available treatment history and documented missed appointments


-


Future medical expense extraction for damages work and settlement positioning


**Reported Client Outcomes:**


Codes Health publishes company-reported figures of[80% less manual review](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) ,[2.5x faster retrieval workflows](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) , and[50% more capacity](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) . The cited page does not disclose the measurement methodology or comparison baseline, and individual results may vary.


**Turnaround and Completeness:**


Codes Health advertises average retrieval in a couple of weeks, with completeness checks and missing-record detection. It checks returned materials against original requests and works with facilities to resolve identified gaps before returning completed record sets. Timing and available documentation depend on the request.


**Catching Authorization Errors Early:**


Incomplete authorizations are a leading preventable cause of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can delay disclosure and force a resubmission. Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections.


**Pricing Model:**


Codes Health uses flat-fee pricing. Confirm included analysis services, request scope, and any additional charges in the service agreement. Bundled chronology services may reduce separate purchasing needs, depending on the firm's review requirements.


**Integration and Workflow:**


The Codes Health[Filevine partnership](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/filevine) , announced July 13, 2026, lets firms initiate requests, track progress, communicate with the Codes Health team, and receive completed records directly within their case files. For high-volume customers, Codes Health builds custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software.


**Best For:**


-


Complex medical malpractice cases requiring care-focused analysis


-


Mass tort practices needing consistent chronologies across plaintiff portfolios


-


High-volume personal injury firms looking to cut manual review time


-


Firms wanting to reduce separate chronology vendor relationships

## **Understanding the Value of AI-Powered Medical Record Analysis**

Codes Health's AI platform is built to analyze medical records with high precision for legal use cases, paired with human review.


**What Purpose-Built AI Delivers:**

-

-

-


Documented missed appointments surfaced for review


-


Flags for apparent gaps in the available treatment history


-


Future expense identification from physician recommendations


**Why Human Verification Matters:**


AI-generated insights require validation before use in litigation. Codes Health combines purpose-built medical-record analysis with human review by medical and legal specialists. AI-generated findings should still be checked against the source records before use in litigation.


Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team continuously builds out additional workflows and products, so the platform keeps evolving, improving, and becoming more comprehensive to meet the changing demands of modern legal practices.

## **Completeness vs. Same-Day Speed**


Same-day retrieval sounds appealing, but speed and completeness are separate evaluation criteria. Codes Health's position is that services offering same-day retrieval often don't get the complete records, and when gaps surface later, firms can face:


-


Settlement delays when missing records surface during demand preparation


-


Expert review complications when incomplete files require re-retrieval


-


Defense arguments about inadequate documentation


-


Client frustration and churn when cases stall over record gaps


**How Codes Health Approaches Completeness:**


Codes Health uses AI-assisted validation to[check delivered records](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) against original requests. When records appear incomplete, the service works with facilities to resolve identified gaps before returning completed sets, so firms know what's been checked rather than hoping providers sent everything needed.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What are the main types of medical record retrieval services available today?**


Medical record retrieval services fall into three broad categories: traditional vendors that handle manual request and follow-up processes, portal-dependent services that provide fast access through electronic health record connections, and AI-powered platforms that combine retrieval with analysis features. Many providers now add some analysis, and[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) brings retrieval, chronologies, potential breach-of-care flags, and missing record identification together in one workflow.


### **How does AI improve the speed and accuracy of medical record retrieval?**


AI supports retrieval through pre-submission authorization checks that catch errors before they cause rejections, automated follow-up across multiple channels, and completeness checks comparing returned records against original requests. For analysis, AI extracts structured information from unstructured clinical notes, identifies treatment patterns, and flags case-relevant facts. General AI platforms like ChatGPT aren't designed for litigation-grade medical record review, while Codes Health's purpose-built platform pairs high-precision analysis with human review. Findings should still be checked against source records.


### **Can I integrate medical record retrieval directly into my case management system?**


Yes, though integration depth varies. Codes Health offers a[dedicated Filevine partnership](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/filevine) that embeds retrieval directly into case files, plus custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software for high-volume customers. Records On Time provides integrations with 7 CMS platforms. When evaluating options, consider whether the connection supports request initiation, status tracking, team communication, and record delivery, or only document transfer.


### **How do medical record retrieval services ensure the completeness of records?**


Approaches vary, so ask each vendor how it checks requested providers, date ranges, and record types, and how it handles missing materials. Codes Health uses AI-assisted validation to compare returned materials against original requests, identify missing facilities or date ranges, and work with providers to resolve gaps before delivery, which reduces the chance of[discovering gaps late](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) during settlement preparation.


### **Are there specific retrieval solutions tailored for personal injury or medical malpractice cases?**


Codes Health serves seven legal practice areas: personal injury, mass torts, medical malpractice, workers' compensation, disability law, insurance litigation, and wrongful death. The platform tailors analysis to each practice area. Personal injury cases get treatment-gap and damages-focused analysis, while medical malpractice cases get potential breach-of-care flags for expert review, producing[case-specific insights](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) rather than generic summaries.


### **What should I look for in a HIPAA-compliant medical record retrieval provider?**


Beyond basic HIPAA compliance, evaluate providers for encryption standards (AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit), audit trail capabilities, access controls, and monitoring practices. Consider whether the provider's AI features use client data for model training.[Codes Health states](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) that client data is not used to train its models. For enterprise procurement, request security documentation including SOC 2 reports, penetration testing summaries, and business associate agreement terms.
